reading.body:
CyrusOne's Austin campus publishes 19 MW of IT load, which is small next to the gigawatt-scale footprints now associated with AI training hubs.

The facility pairs that capacity with 242,000 square feet of technical space and a compliance stack covering PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942. That combination points to regulated enterprise workloads in finance, healthcare, and federal use rather than unconstrained AI training spend. The certifications are the differentiator here, not the megawatts.

Within Texas the campus ranks tenth by published capacity among 19 facilities that disclose figures, about 4 percent of the state's 475 MW of published IT load. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, and most publish nothing, so the ranking describes a subset of supply rather than the market. The 19 MW is a published ceiling, not a measure of available headroom.

What the data does not cover is decisive for AI planning. Power delivery headroom, grid interconnection quality, and whether the shell can support GPU densities above legacy IT are all unpublished. A reader should treat 19 MW as the top of the range this facility has stated, and nothing more.
